messages:
maya: Heads-up: noticing ~10-25% tail latency on FP8 path on H100 when L40S kernels are picked for short batch shapes (seq ~32, batch 1-8). Starts after KV hot-cache flushes. Telemetry trace: https://go/trace/abc123 :thinking_face:

devon: Can you paste the sampled kernel selection dump? Is it nvfuser vs transformer-engine path?

maya: quick dump: `kernel=te_l40s_fp8_sel, batch=4, seq=32, kernel_latency_ms=1.8, fallback_to_nvfuser=false` then next req `kernel=nvfuser_int8, latency_ms=2.6` — seems jittery

liam: From perf traces, selector uses seq_estimator based on prefix lengths, but when KV warmup causes prefixes to be replayed we get incorrect shape hist and the selector flips path mid-stream. Attaching small snippet: ```selector:hist{seq: [32:60%, 512:30%, 16:10%]} samples=1200```

anika: Hypothesis: padding/truncation during batching leads TE kernels to assume packed small seqs -> FP8 path, but on H100 TE FP8 shows higher variance when occupancy is low. Two quick mitigations: 1) prefer nvfuser for batch<8 & seq<64; 2) add sticky-kernel for warmup requests.

maya: @anika sounds good. Can we opt-in a sticky-kernel heuristic in runtime? Where would we toggle?

anika: There's a flag in runtime config: `runtime.kernel_selection.sticky_enabled=true` and `runtime.kernel_selection.min_sticky_requests=20`. Also try `transformer_engine.force_fp8_check=false` to avoid aggressive FP8 path if suboptimal.

runtime-bot: deploy queued: roll:kernel-selector/2026-03-18T14:20 (canary -> 10% nodes).

devon: Before deploy: increase telemetry sample rate for kernel decisions to 10% (was 1%) so we can validate. Also add trace id to hotpath logs.

liam: Agree. Also add a micro-benchmark: sweep microbatches (batch 1-16, seq 8-128) on the h100-l40s image and compare fp8 vs nvfuser latency & p50/p95.

maya: I'll run the sweep later today and post results. If we see >15% p95 regression we rollback. Thanks :thumbsup:
